citation: Denes and van Sebille (2024). Plasticparcels. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.07094
description: Plasticparcels is the Parcels team's Python package for simulating transport and dispersion of plastic particles in the ocean. It builds on the Parcels particle-tracking engine and supplies physical kernels for current advection, Stokes drift, wind-induced motion, biofouling, vertical mixing and sea-ice capture. Inputs include particle properties, release scenarios, environmental fields and JSON settings; outputs describe simulated trajectories over the chosen domain and period. Public source and documentation are free under MIT. A limitation is that hydrodynamic, biogeochemical, wind and wave inputs come from separate providers, and available processes depend on selected kernels and forcing resolution. The published examples require local data paths or compatible streamed inputs. Plasticparcels can support waste-dispersal and marine-cleanup simulations, complementary to Delft3D FM (model-delft3d-fm) for coastal hydrodynamics. Its documentation cites the 2024 JOSS paper and explains alternative input arrangements. No forcing datasets, initial particle maps or simulated trajectories were downloaded.
